literal: Subordinate-Domain Military Prefectures
idiomatic: Subordinate-Domain Military Prefectures (touxia junzhou)

literal: Subordinate-domain military prefectures were all set up by princes, maternal kin, great ministers, and various divisions from campaign captives or purchased persons, each gathered to build prefectures and counties to dwell.
idiomatic: Subordinate-domain prefectures arose when princes, imperial kin, ministers, and tribal divisions settled campaign captives or purchased persons in grouped prefectures and counties.

literal: Horizontal-Tent princes, imperial maternal uncles, and princesses might found walled prefectures; others might not build cities.
idiomatic: Horizontal-Tent princes, imperial uncles, and princesses could raise walled prefectures; others could not.

literal: The court bestowed prefecture and county names.

literal: Military commissioners were court-appointed; cishi and below were all filled from the founder's tribal followers.
idiomatic: Military commissioners came from the throne; prefects and lower ranks were drawn from the founder's own followers.

literal: Official posts below the nine grades and market households' taxes all returned to the head;
idiomatic: Taxes from sub-ninth-rank offices and market households went to the domain head;

literal: only liquor tax was paid to Shangjing's Salt and Iron Office.
idiomatic: only liquor tax went to Shangjing's Salt and Iron Office.
